title: Lena and the Signal
premise: Lior Reyes, a xenolinguist whose mind has been reshaped by decades of translating alien signal patterns, serves as the sole interpreter keeping an uneasy truce between two human fleets on the edge of the Meridian Expanse. When the ship Vespera returns from deep space carrying a crew aged backward into childhood, Lior realizes the 'alien threat' both fleets fear is a fabrication they themselves helped maintain. As the child-crew's memories surface in fragments of a language that predates both fleets, Lior must choose between preserving the lie that keeps the peace or revealing a truth that could unite—or shatter—them all, ultimately broadcasting the real signal and finding belonging not in either fleet but among those who, like them, no longer fit anywhere.
about_author: L. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years relaying messages between ships that rarely answered. They write about language, distance, and the families people build in transit.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Lior's POV aboard the relay vessel Quiet Hours, translating routine fleet traffic between the Concord and the Halcyon Compact. We learn Lior dreams in static and alien phonemes now, not human words—a private shame. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence; Lior is indispensable and utterly alone.

chapters.title: Vespera Returns
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The deep-space ship Vespera docks at neutral station Threnody, its crew of forty now children under ten, physically unaged for thirty years. Command orders silence pending investigation. Lior is assigned to debrief them—the only linguist who might parse their altered speech. Beat: dread mixed with a flicker of recognition; these children speak fragments of Lior's dream-language.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Lior and Tam, the eldest returned child (biologically seven). Tam describes the Vespera's encounter with something that 'unwound' them, speaking in a cadence Lior knows from intercepted signals. Fleet observers grow suspicious of Lior's rapport with the children. Beat: tentative connection; Lior feels understood for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, flashbacks interleaved. We learn the 'alien threat' justifying the fleets' armed standoff was manufactured decades ago—and Lior's own translations were doctored to sustain it. Their mentor, Admiral Okafor, admits complicity. Beat: betrayal and vertigo; Lior's identity as honest translator collapses.

chapters.title: What the Children Remember
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The children's shared memories surface during sleep—collective dreams of a vast, patient intelligence that didn't attack them but offered communion, which their captains refused in terror. Tam begins teaching the other children the signal-language deliberately. Beat: quiet defiance; the smallest people carry the largest truth.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Both fleets intercept the children's transmissions and interpret them as hostile coordination. War posture escalates; Threnody becomes a bargaining chip. Okafor pressures Lior to produce a 'threatening' translation. Beat: suffocating pressure; Lior must falsify or defect.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Defection
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Lior smuggles the children toward the Vespera while Tam's group decodes the full original message: an invitation, renewable only during a rare alignment weeks away. A loyalist officer discovers them; Lior talks their way past using the signal-language itself, proving it carries no aggression. Beat: terror transformed into conviction.

chapters.title: Alignment
chapters.summary: Lior's POV at the climax. With both fleets converging on Threnody to destroy the Vespera, Lior broadcasts the unaltered signal fleet-wide—every bridge hears the invitation raw. The children add their voices, translating in chorus. Fleets hold fire, paralyzed by doubt. Beat: breathless risk; truth spoken aloud at last.

chapters.title: Answered
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The deep intelligence responds—not to the fleets, but to the children, acknowledging them as its first speakers. The standoff dissolves as both fleets realize their enemy never existed. Some officers refuse the truth; Okafor publicly confesses the fabrication. Beat: awe and grief together; wonder costs something.

chapters.title: A Language to Come Home To
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, months later. Lior stays at Threnody with the children, building the first true human-xeno pidgin, no longer serving either fleet but a new community of translators, returnees, and defectors. Lior finally dreams in a language with words for 'home.' Beat: belonging found not by fitting in, but by making a place where misfits belong.
